DINOv2 Embedding POC — Before Fine-Tuning¶

Goal: evaluate whether pretrained DINOv2 embeddings contain useful patterns for the wheat-grain dataset before any fine-tuning.

This notebook does not train DINOv2 and does not make the final class prediction.

Flow¶

YOLO-Seg labeled dataset → Extract individual grain crops → Pretrained DINOv2 (frozen) → Embeddings → Analyze patterns/separability

What this notebook checks¶

  • Dataset/classes and number of labeled grain instances
  • DINOv2 embeddings for each grain
  • PCA visualization
  • Optional t-SNE visualization
  • Class-centroid cosine similarity
  • Silhouette score
  • Nearest-neighbor same-class consistency
  • Save embeddings for later RF / XGBoost / CatBoost / SVM experiments

Assumption: labels are in YOLO segmentation polygon format.
Class names are read automatically from data.yaml when available.

IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".tif", ".tiff", ".webp"}

def read_class_names(dataset_dir):
    yaml_candidates = list(dataset_dir.glob("*.yaml")) + list(dataset_dir.glob("*.yml"))
    for yp in yaml_candidates:
        try:
            cfg = yaml.safe_load(yp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            names = cfg.get("names")
            if isinstance(names, list):
                return {i: name for i, name in enumerate(names)}, yp
            if isinstance(names, dict):
                return {int(k): v for k, v in names.items()}, yp
        except Exception:
            pass
    return {}, None

CLASS_NAMES, YAML_PATH = read_class_names(DATASET_DIR)

print("data.yaml:", YAML_PATH)
print("Classes  :", CLASS_NAMES if CLASS_NAMES else "Not found; class IDs will still be parsed.")

In [7]:
def find_split_pairs(dataset_dir):
    split_aliases = [("train", "train"), ("valid", "valid"), ("val", "val"), ("test", "test")]
    found = []

    # Layout A: root/train/images + root/train/labels
    for split_name, folder in split_aliases:
        img_dir = dataset_dir / folder / "images"
        lbl_dir = dataset_dir / folder / "labels"
        if img_dir.exists() and lbl_dir.exists():
            found.append((split_name, img_dir, lbl_dir))

    # Layout B: root/images/train + root/labels/train
    for split_name, folder in split_aliases:
        img_dir = dataset_dir / "images" / folder
        lbl_dir = dataset_dir / "labels" / folder
        if img_dir.exists() and lbl_dir.exists():
            candidate = (split_name, img_dir, lbl_dir)
            if candidate not in found:
                found.append(candidate)

    return found

SPLIT_DIRS = find_split_pairs(DATASET_DIR)

if not SPLIT_DIRS:

5. Parse YOLO segmentation labels — one record per grain¶

In [8]:
def parse_yolo_segmentation_line(line):
    parts = line.strip().split()
    if len(parts) < 7:  # class + at least 3 polygon points
        return None

    class_id = int(float(parts[0]))
    coords = np.array([float(v) for v in parts[1:]], dtype=np.float32)

    if len(coords) % 2 != 0:
        return None

    polygon = coords.reshape(-1, 2)
    return class_id, polygon


records = []

for split_name, img_dir, lbl_dir in SPLIT_DIRS:
    image_paths = [p for p in img_dir.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS]

    for image_path in tqdm(image_paths, desc=f"Reading {split_name}"):
        label_path = lbl_dir / f"{image_path.stem}.txt"

        if not label_path.exists():
            rel = image_path.relative_to(img_dir).with_suffix(".txt")
            label_path = lbl_dir / rel

        if not label_path.exists():
            continue

        try:
            with Image.open(image_path) as im:
                width, height = im.size
        except Exception:
            continue

        lines = label_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").splitlines()

        for instance_idx, line in enumerate(lines):
            parsed = parse_yolo_segmentation_line(line)
            if parsed is None:
                continue

            class_id, polygon_norm = parsed

            polygon_px = polygon_norm.copy()
            polygon_px[:, 0] *= width
            polygon_px[:, 1] *= height

            records.append({
                "split": split_name,
                "image_path": str(image_path),
                "label_path": str(label_path),
                "instance_idx": instance_idx,
                "class_id": class_id,
                "class_name": CLASS_NAMES.get(class_id, f"class_{class_id}"),
                "polygon_px": polygon_px,
                "image_width": width,
                "image_height": height,
            })

instances_df = pd.DataFrame(records)

if len(instances_df) == 0:
    raise ValueError(
        "No YOLO segmentation instances were parsed. "
        "Check that your .txt labels contain polygon coordinates, not only bounding boxes."
    )

print("Grain labels :", len(instances_df))

display(

6. Extract individual grain crops¶

In [11]:
def extract_grain_crop(
    image_path,
    polygon_px,
    crop_mode="masked",
    padding_ratio=0.08,
    background_value=127,
):
    image_bgr = cv2.imread(str(image_path), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
    if image_bgr is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not read image: {image_path}")

    image_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(image_bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    h, w = image_rgb.shape[:2]

    polygon = np.round(np.asarray(polygon_px)).astype(np.int32)

    x, y, bw, bh = cv2.boundingRect(polygon)
    pad_x = int(bw * padding_ratio)
    pad_y = int(bh * padding_ratio)

    x1 = max(0, x - pad_x)
    y1 = max(0, y - pad_y)
    x2 = min(w, x + bw + pad_x)
    y2 = min(h, y + bh + pad_y)

    crop = image_rgb[y1:y2, x1:x2].copy()

    if crop_mode == "bbox":
        return Image.fromarray(crop)

    poly_local = polygon.copy()
    poly_local[:, 0] -= x1
    poly_local[:, 1] -= y1

    mask = np.zeros(crop.shape[:2], dtype=np.uint8)
    cv2.fillPoly(mask, [poly_local], 255)

    background = np.full_like(crop, background_value)
    masked = np.where(mask[..., None] > 0, crop, background)

    return Image.fromarray(masked)

8. DINOv2 preprocessing¶

In [18]:
# Baseline: only the preprocessing expected by the pretrained model.
# No extra color-normalization experiment is applied here.

dino_transform = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize(
        (IMAGE_SIZE, IMAGE_SIZE),
        interpolation=transforms.InterpolationMode.BICUBIC
    ),
    transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize(
        mean=(0.485, 0.456, 0.406),
        std=(0.229, 0.224, 0.225),
    ),
])

9. Build DataLoader¶

In [19]:
class GrainCropDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, dataframe):
        self.df = dataframe.reset_index(drop=True)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.df)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        row = self.df.iloc[idx]

        crop = extract_grain_crop(
            row["image_path"],
            row["polygon_px"],
            crop_mode=CROP_MODE,
            padding_ratio=PADDING_RATIO,
            background_value=MASK_BACKGROUND,
        )

        tensor = dino_transform(crop)

        meta = {
            "split": row["split"],
            "image_path": row["image_path"],
            "instance_idx": int(row["instance_idx"]),
            "class_id": int(row["class_id"]),
            "class_name": row["class_name"],
        }
        return tensor, meta


grain_ds = GrainCropDataset(instances_df)

grain_loader = DataLoader(
    grain_ds,
    batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    shuffle=False,
    num_workers=0,     # Windows/Jupyter-friendly
    pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
)

print("Number of grain instances:", len(grain_ds))

10. Extract pretrained DINOv2 embeddings¶

In [20]:
all_embeddings = []
all_meta = []

use_amp = DEVICE == "cuda"

with torch.inference_mode():
    for images, meta in tqdm(grain_loader, desc="DINOv2 embeddings"):
        images = images.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)

        if use_amp:
            with torch.autocast(device_type="cuda", dtype=torch.float16):
                features = model.forward_features(images)
                emb = features["x_norm_clstoken"]
        else:
            features = model.forward_features(images)
            emb = features["x_norm_clstoken"]

        all_embeddings.append(emb.float().cpu().numpy())

        batch_len = len(meta["class_id"])
        for i in range(batch_len):
            all_meta.append({
                "split": meta["split"][i],
                "image_path": meta["image_path"][i],
                "instance_idx": int(meta["instance_idx"][i]),
                "class_id": int(meta["class_id"][i]),
                "class_name": meta["class_name"][i],
            })

embeddings = np.concatenate(all_embeddings, axis=0)

print("Embedding matrix shape:", embeddings.shape)
print("Embedding dimension   :", embeddings.shape[1])

if len(meta_df) > MAX_PLOT_SAMPLES:
    sample_idx = np.random.default_rng(RANDOM_STATE).choice(

perplexity = min(30, max(5, (len(X_50) - 1) // 3))

    n_components=2,
    perplexity=perplexity,
    init="pca",
    learning_rate="auto",
    random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
)

14. Quantitative class-separability checks¶

In [25]:
labels = meta_df["class_id"].to_numpy()
unique_labels = np.unique(labels)

if len(unique_labels) >= 2:
    if len(emb_l2) > 5000:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(RANDOM_STATE)
        sil_idx = rng.choice(len(emb_l2), 5000, replace=False)
        sil = silhouette_score(
            emb_l2[sil_idx],
            labels[sil_idx],
            metric="cosine",
        )
    else:
        sil = silhouette_score(
            emb_l2,
            labels,
            metric="cosine",
        )

    print(f"Silhouette score (cosine): {sil:.4f}")
    print("Higher is better; values near 0 indicate strong overlap.")
else:
    print("Silhouette score requires at least 2 classes.")

Class-centroid cosine similarity¶

In [26]:
centroids = []
centroid_names = []

for class_id, grp in meta_df.groupby("class_id"):
    idx = grp.index.to_numpy()

    centroid = emb_l2[idx].mean(axis=0)
    centroid = centroid / (np.linalg.norm(centroid) + 1e-12)

    centroids.append(centroid)
    centroid_names.append(
        CLASS_NAMES.get(int(class_id), f"class_{class_id}")
    )

centroids = np.stack(centroids)
sim_matrix = cosine_similarity(centroids)

sim_df = pd.DataFrame(
    sim_matrix,
    index=centroid_names,
    columns=centroid_names,
)

display(sim_df.round(3))

print(
    "\nInterpretation: closer to 1 = more similar class centroids. "
    "Lower off-diagonal values suggest better separation."
)

Nearest-neighbor label consistency¶

In [27]:
# This does not train a classifier.
# It only checks whether nearby embeddings often share the same known label.

nn_limit = min(5000, len(emb_l2))
rng = np.random.default_rng(RANDOM_STATE)

if len(emb_l2) > nn_limit:
    nn_idx = rng.choice(len(emb_l2), nn_limit, replace=False)
else:
    nn_idx = np.arange(len(emb_l2))

X_nn = emb_l2[nn_idx]
y_nn = labels[nn_idx]

sim = cosine_similarity(X_nn)
np.fill_diagonal(sim, -np.inf)

nearest = sim.argmax(axis=1)
same_class_rate = (y_nn[nearest] == y_nn).mean()

print(f"Nearest-neighbor same-class rate: {same_class_rate:.4f}")

Nearest-neighbor same-class rate: 0.8448

15. How to interpret the POC¶

We are not expecting perfect separation from pretrained DINOv2.

We are checking whether the embedding space contains useful structure:

  • Good sign: same-class grains tend to stay close.
  • Good sign: classes show visible separation in PCA/t-SNE.
  • Good sign: positive silhouette score and useful nearest-neighbor consistency.
  • Warning: classes completely overlap even when labels are reliable.
  • Warning: embeddings cluster mainly by lighting/background/session instead of grain class.

Recommended next experiments¶

  1. Keep this as the pretrained baseline.
  2. Compare masked crop vs bbox crop.
  3. Compare DINOv2-S vs DINOv2-B.
  4. Test blur / lower resolution.
  5. Test original vs color-normalized images separately.
  6. If needed, compare with fine-tuned DINOv2 embeddings later.
  7. Feed saved embeddings into RF / XGBoost / CatBoost / SVM as a separate downstream experiment.

When you later train/evaluate ML models, avoid randomly mixing consecutive frames from the same recording across Train/Test. Split by recording/session/batch to reduce data leakage.
